A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RenderFlow by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated appendix content.

before.justification: V1 reports original forward- and inverse-rendering evaluations, quantitative ablations, keyframe-gap experiments, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds an input-buffer ablation and further inference-step examples.

M1.justification: The proposed flow model, adapters, losses, and inference procedures are unchanged. Appendix A.3 tests Albedo×Irradiance as an ablation but explicitly retains the original albedo input for the main experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Unreal Engine synthetic and artist-crafted scene coverage for forward rendering, intrinsic decomposition, and material editing. The added buffer comparison and illustrative cases do not establish a new dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: RGB-X and DiffusionRenderer remain the neural comparators in the corresponding forward and inverse evaluations. Table 1 retains the same traditional-rendering entries. The new buffer experiment compares internal variants rather than adding an external baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 introduces an additional protocol comparing two input representations, each trained at low resolution for one day. Existing main-experiment splits, metrics, training budgets, and baseline sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an ablation testing whether multiplying albedo by irradiance improves reconstruction. Appendix D and Figure 11 also extend the existing inference-step analysis with two cases favoring four steps. The earlier keyframe, loss, architecture, and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains evaluation over a 100-frame sequence averaged across 10 runs, with shaded variance. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance testing is introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 23.7/0.75/0.13 for albedo and 25.6/0.76/0.13 for Albedo×Irradiance. New Figure 11 examples report one-step versus four-step PSNRs of 29.3 versus 30.2 and 24.8 versus 25.5. Tables 1–5 and the keyframe-gap results, renumbered from Table 6 to Table 7, are unchanged; these are additional findings, not improved main-benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The bridge/flow formulations and rendering losses in Equations 1–12 are unchanged. The new appendix material adds empirical analysis and interpretation, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about deterministic single-step rendering, improved quality and efficiency, sparse-keyframe guidance, and unified forward/inverse rendering.

C2.justification: Appendix D now acknowledges that four-step inference can outperform one step when generated details align with ground truth. Appendix A.3 interprets irradiance as a useful prior and explains retaining albedo for comparison fairness. The dedicated limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents one-day, low-resolution training for the new buffer ablation. Conversely, Figure 11's revised caption removes the earlier explicit statement that inference-step tests used no keyframes; this is a disclosure loss, not evidence of a changed setting. Existing implementation and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly credits RGB-X for using target-attribute text embeddings, and A.3 relates the retained input choice to DiffusionRenderer. The bibliography and main related-work discussion otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 corrects several spelling and grammatical errors, adds the short Input Buffer Selection subsection, and expands the inference-step discussion. The main narrative and section ordering are retained without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V2 adds a buffer-comparison table, expands and relocates Figure 11, makes small architecture-diagram updates, and reflows the appendix. The existing keyframe table is renumbered, and Figures 14–16 move to later pages without new result content.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves empirical scrutiny through the input-buffer ablation and examples qualifying single-step superiority. These additions make the analysis more informative without changing the main results. The gain is limited: Appendix D retains an overly broad statement that single-step inference consistently wins, and Figure 11 loses its explicit no-keyframe qualifier.
